newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Inflation confidence expressed in yield spread-RBA.
newsitem.headline: Inflation confidence expressed in yield spread-RBA.

text.p: The narrow long-term yield spread Australia and the U.S. suggests confidence that Australia will sustain the recent performance on inflation beyond the medium term, the Reserve Bank of Australia said in its August bulletim.

The differential between 10-year bond yields in the U.S. fell to around 35 basis points last month, below the spread at the low-point in Australian bond yields in January 1994 and the lowest level since August 1984.
"The current slim spread, however, signifies a much healthier state of affairs than the situation of the mid 1980's," the central bank Said.
"In 1984, bond yields both in the United States and Australia were around 13-14 percent, with U.S. yields having increased as U.S. inflation expectations deteriorated," it said.
"The recent experience has seen bond yields in Australia fall toward those in the United States, based on comparably low inflation rates," the RBA added.
Australian annual headline inflation was 0.3 percent in the second quarter compared with annual U.S. inflation of 2.2 percent.

It noted the short end of the curve for maturities of less that five years had moved below that segment of the U.S., being heavily influenced by the stance of monetary policy and the relative position of the two economies at present, with Australia in a weaker phase than the U.S.
Current Australian official rates are 5.0 percent compared with 5.5 percent in the U.S.
"The long end of the curve is determined by the market's expectations about economic performance and inflation likely to be achieved over the longer haul," the RBA said.
"The narrow differential between long-term bond yields in Australia and the U.S. suggests confidence that Australia will sustain the recent performance on inflation beyond the medium term," it said.

"The experience of 1994 suggests, however, that such confidence might prove fragile if there were much slippage on the inflation front, or if world bond market conditions in general were to deteriorate," it added.
